interpretation.headline: NEGATIVE RESULT about the full-window estimator: its leakage model over-predicts by at least 1.23 +- 0.23 states.
interpretation.why_this_is_a_bound_not_an_estimate: deflated = leakage + missed with both terms non-negative, so a deflated measurement of 2.52 against a predicted leakage of 3.75 means the model over-predicts by AT LEAST 1.23; if the I1 slice also missed states, the over-prediction is larger still. The true population of [1.70129, 2.15583] cannot be counted here because prod_N1000_G128 was moved off this filesystem, so 'missed' is not separable from model bias.
interpretation.cleanest_possible_test: No grid confound: the KPM moments (kpm_n1000_G128_prod_kpm.npz) and the solve share structure, decoration, grid 128^3 and lam_max (4633.5995 vs 4633.6). The N=10k window used a 256^3 DOS against a 192^3 solve; here that excuse is unavailable and the bias persists.
interpretation.does_NOT_touch_the_N10k_certification: The N=10k gate was certified on the SUB-INTERVAL, where the true leakage is 0.0017 -- three orders below this bias -- so the certifying number does not depend on the leakage model at all. This is precisely why Amendment A3 made the sub-interval the certifying test and demoted the full window to a consistency check. The calibration confirms that call was right, and confirms the full-window number (+1.68 +- 0.32 at N=10k) must not be read as a state count.
interpretation.sign_differs_from_N10k: calibration -1.23, N=10k window +1.68 -- opposite signs, so this is not a constant offset that could be subtracted off. Not modelled further.

partial_coverage.reading: all 18 unconverged states lie within 0.025 of a window edge (12 at the 1.80 floor, 6 at the 2.06 ceiling) while every converged state is >= 0.0084 inside. This is the bandpass filter's transition zone: edge states receive the least amplification and converge slowest. The usable 160^3 result is therefore an INTERIOR sub-window [1.8096, 2.0516], which is what any 160-vs-192 comparison must be restricted to.

IMPACT ON THE SEAM VERDICT.unaffected: The POSITIVE half stands: six montage bulk states have periodic partners at overlap 0.95-0.9997 with Delta-lambda all negative. Finding a partner is positive evidence and incompleteness cannot manufacture it.
IMPACT ON THE SEAM VERDICT.WEAKENED: The NEGATIVE half -- 'the four seam-flagged states vanished' -- rested on those states having no partner above 0.5 among the seven converged periodic states. With the periodic solve now measured to be missing ~1 state in the sub-interval alone (and ~4 across the window), ABSENCE OF A PARTNER IS NOT PROOF OF ABSENCE. The seam states are still the best explanation, but the test no longer excludes the alternative that they persist and were simply not found.

Bulk states shifted -0.0007..-0.0034 and the band-edge state shifted -0.0248; a state living in the very shell whose material changed would be expected to shift hard. So 1.9095 is a plausible heavily-shifted counterpart of a seam state. NOT TESTABLE from stored data: run_interior.py saves only converged pairs, and the checkpoint holding that vector was removed under the approved post-save cleanup policy. Deciding it needs a re-solve with more polish outers.

I8 localization (cross-solver xi agreeme.note: restricted to modes resolved in both: an unresolved fit is a lower bound and comparing it would be meaningless. In an 11.44 um box the L/2 = 5.72 um ceiling catches most modes, so this is a small but honest sample.
I8 localization (cross-solver xi agreeme.honest_caveat: The agreement is 0.01-0.09%, i.e. far tighter than the 10% gate, and that tightness should be read for what it is. The two solvers agree on these eigenvalues to ~3e-07 with near-unit eigenvector overlap (gate I4), so they hand the localization pipeline almost the SAME field. What this therefore establishes strongly is that the pipeline is deterministic and free of solver-path dependence -- it does NOT independently validate the envelope-fit METHOD itself, since both numbers come from the same estimator. The method's own fit-range sensitivity was measured separately in adversarial round 3 (item 3): absolute xi moves at the tens-of-percent level as the fit range varies, while the trend survives. Both facts belong in the report.
I8 localization (cross-solver xi agreeme.sample_restriction: 20 of 216 modes. 210 matched across solvers; 42 were resolved in BOTH (the L/2 = 5.72 um ceiling in an 11.44 um box catches the rest); 20 of those sit within 0.15 of a gap edge. Comparing unresolved fits was refused because a ceiling-limited xi is a lower bound, not a value.

HEADLINE.reading: BOTH grids converge exactly 11 states in [1.84, 1.95]. This is the first direct evidence that the in-gap states are NOT manufactured by coarse rasterization -- a 1.33x finer grid (7.79 -> 10.39 vox/um, 2.4x the voxels) neither creates nor destroys states here.

eigenvalue_shift.reading: median -0.26%, 9 of 11 negative. Downward is the physically expected direction: a finer grid resolves more dielectric, and more dielectric lowers frequencies.

CAVEAT_matching.reading: The typical inter-grid shift is 3.2x the SMALLEST level spacing in this window, so pairing states between grids by sorted order is NOT reliable -- states can reorder. The COUNT agreement is robust to this; the per-state pairing above is not, and no per-state claim is made from it. A rigorous match would embed the 192^3 spectral coefficients into the 256^3 basis by zero-padding (Fourier interpolation) and use eigenvector overlap, as the seam test did within one grid. NOT DONE.
